title: Character reconstruction of relative tori from etale lattice sheaves
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Use its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and sheaves of abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. A lattice sheaf $\mathcal M$ means a sheaf which is etale locally isomorphic to a constant sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z^r}$ for some finite $r\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]; the rank may vary between connected components. For a scheme $T$ write $\mathbf G_{m,T}$ for the group scheme obtained by gluing $\operatorname{Spec}A[t,t^{-1}]$ over affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$, with comultiplication $t\mapsto t\otimes t$, counit $t\mapsto1$, and inverse $t\mapsto t^{-1}$. A torus over $S$ means a commutative $S$-group scheme (with multiplication, inverse and unit satisfying the group diagrams) which is fppf locally [def-pc-fppf-site] isomorphic to $\mathbf G_{m,S}^r$, locally on $S$, for finite $r$. For an $S$-group scheme $P$, let $X^*(P)$ be the etale sheaf $U\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{U\text{-grp}}(P\times_SU,\mathbf G_{m,U})$.

The functor $X^*$ is a contravariant equivalence between tori over $S$ and lattice sheaves. A quasi-inverse sends $\mathcal M$ to the scheme $D_S(\mathcal M)$ representing the functor on $S$-schemes
$$T\longmapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Ab}(T_{\mathrm{et}})}(\mathcal M|_T,\mathbf G_{m,T}),$$
where $\mathcal M|_T$ is the ordinary etale inverse image sheaf [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and the second argument denotes the units sheaf of the displayed group scheme. There are natural identifications $X^*(D_S(\mathcal M))\simeq\mathcal M$ and $D_S(X^*(P))\simeq P$. The construction and these identifications commute with arbitrary scheme base change [def-pc-base-change]. If $\mathcal M|_U\simeq\underline{\mathbf Z^r}$ then $D_S(\mathcal M)\times_SU\simeq\mathbf G_{m,U}^r$. The structure map $D_S(\mathcal M)\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], affine, faithfully flat and of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; affine means that inverse images of affine opens are affine. Over every algebraically closed geometric point $s$ its fibre is $\mathbf G_{m,s}^r$, where $r=\operatorname{rank}\mathcal M_s$. Rank zero is included.

source.place: Lan, §3.1.1, Definitions 3.1.1.1, 3.1.1.4–5 and Lemma 3.1.1.6; online revised thesis printed p.61 read. Explicit relative representability and smooth affine finite-presentation properties from the local split model; local text WANTED.

proof.text: For the split model, the relative matrix lemma identifies $X^*(\mathbf G_{m,B}^r)$ with $\underline{\mathbf Z^r}$ and identifies its automorphism sheaf on arbitrary test schemes with locally constant $\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbf Z)$-valued maps. The constant-sheaf sections lemma identifies integer-matrix functions with sections of the constant additive matrix sheaf; invertibility is the pointwise condition of lying in $\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbf Z)$. A homomorphism between finite free constant abelian sheaves is determined by the images of the finitely many standard generators: locally these images form an integer matrix, and every such matrix defines a homomorphism. Thus the contravariant correspondence on split models is exactly precomposition of characters, with composition and addition as in the matrix lemma. This uses locally constant matrices, not a single matrix on a possibly disconnected base.

proof.text: Let $P$ be an fppf torus, trivialized on $U_i$ with ranks $r_i$. On a nonempty overlap the two ranks agree at every geometric point: the split matrix lemma gives inverse maps between $\mathbf Z^{r_i}$ and $\mathbf Z^{r_j}$; reducing modulo $2$ gives $2^{r_i}=2^{r_j}$. The labelled-clopen descent lemma descends the rank labels to clopen subsets of $S$. Its fpqc hypothesis holds because on each affine open the fppf affine-refinement lemma supplies a finite jointly surjective affine refinement. Work on one rank-$r$ subset. The functor $I(T)=\operatorname{Isom}_{T\text{-grp}}(\mathbf G_{m,T}^r,P_T)$ is an fppf sheaf: compatible maps and inverse maps descend by representable fpqc descent, and their group equations are tested on the pulled-back covers. A chosen frame identifies $I|_{U_i}$ with $\coprod_{\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathbf Z)}U_i$ by Step 1. Fppf-local algebraic-space representability therefore applies, with this set-indexed coproduct as charts in the chosen universe. The projection $I\to S$ is etale by fppf descent of etaleness, applied to the surjective flat locally finitely presented map $\coprod U_i\to S$. It is surjective: a geometric point lifts after field extension to a trivializing cover and then to its identity frame. The smooth-surjection sections lemma, etale being smooth of relative dimension zero, supplies an etale covering of $S$ with frames. Hence $P$ is etale locally split and $X^*(P)$ is a lattice by Step 1.

source.place: 04SK, lemma-locally-algebraic-space; spaces-descent.tex 042B, lemma-descending-property-etale; spaces-topologies.tex 0CFV; agent application to the frame sheaf.

proof.text: Choose an etale cover $U_i\to S$ and trivializations $\mathcal M|_{U_i}\cong\underline{\mathbf Z^{r_i}}$. On overlaps let $a_{ij}$ take coordinates in frame $i$ to coordinates in frame $j$, so $a_{jk}a_{ij}=a_{ik}$. A tuple of units defines a functional on these coordinates. Transport it from $i$ to $j$ by $h\mapsto h\circ a_{ij}^{-1}$. Step 1 represents this transport by an isomorphism between the split tori. The displayed cocycle gives the scheme descent cocycle. On each affine open $V\subset S$, choose a finite affine refinement of the cover; its coproduct $W\to V$ is a flat surjective map between affine schemes. The disjoint union of split models over its components is affine over $W$. Effective affine descent gives a $V$-scheme with these models; affineness descends from $W$. The descended multiplication, identity and inverse exist by morphism descent, since the transition maps are group maps; their diagrams hold because they hold after pullback. For two such local models, morphism descent gives the unique comparison inducing the prescribed transitions. These comparisons satisfy the cocycle, and Zariski gluing gives a commutative $S$-group scheme $D$. No intersection of affine opens is presumed affine: comparisons restrict to an affine cover of the intersection and glue uniquely.

source.place: 0245, lemma-affine; 02W0, lemma-refine-coverings-fully-faithful; 02L5, lemma-descending-property-affine. Agent application to the inverse-dual frame cocycle.

proof.text: Over each affine open $V\subset S$, the affine pieces $V_j$ of Step 3 are open in $U_{i(j)}\times_SV$, hence etale over $S$, and their images cover $V$; on each of them $D$ is the split model of rank $r_{i(j)}$ and $\mathcal M$ is trivialized by the restricted frame. For an arbitrary $S$-scheme $T$, pull back this etale cover $\{V_j\to S\}$ (over all $V$ and $j$) to $T$. Constant sheaves pull back to constant sheaves, so on each pulled-back chart a sheaf homomorphism $\mathcal M|_T\to\mathbf G_{m,T}$ is precisely an $r_i$-tuple of units: by the sheafification universal property, a map from $\underline{\mathbf Z^{r_i}}$ is uniquely specified by the images of its basis, and the split point formula represents these images. On intersections the tuple changes by $h\mapsto h\circ a_{ij}^{-1}$, exactly the transition used for $D$. Maps from sheaves glue uniquely on an etale covering by the sheaf axiom, and maps $T\to D$ glue uniquely by representable fpqc descent (an etale cover is fpqc). Consequently $D(T)$ is naturally the Hom group in the question. These bijections respect the group operations and every test-scheme pullback. This proves representability, and identifies its group law with pointwise multiplication of functionals. It also proves the asserted split model whenever $\mathcal M|_U$ is constant, independently of the originally chosen cover.

proof.text: For a section $m$ of $\mathcal M$, evaluation $h\mapsto h(m)$ defines a character of $D$ and gives $\mathcal M\to X^*(D)$. On every splitting chart this sends the standard basis to the coordinate characters, so Step 1 makes it an isomorphism. For $P$, evaluation sends $p\in P(T)$ to the homomorphism $\chi\mapsto\chi(p)$ from its pulled-back character lattice to the units sheaf. By Step 2 there is an etale splitting cover; on its pullback this map is the identity identification between tuples of units and functionals on $\mathbf Z^r$. Step 4 and Yoneda therefore give an isomorphism $P\to D_S(X^*(P))$: the local inverse scheme maps glue by representable descent, and both inverse identities hold on the cover. For a lattice map $b:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$, define $D(b)(h)=h\circ b$. For a group map $f:P\to Q$, define $X^*(f)(\chi)=\chi\circ f$. The equations $h(b(m))=(h\circ b)(m)$ and $\chi(f(p))=(\chi\circ f)(p)$ prove naturality of the two evaluation maps. They give the claimed contravariant equivalence, with every clause on morphisms included.

source.place: Agent relative descent argument, using Lemma 12.4 and Theorem 12.9(a), pp.232–234; Lan §3.1.1 local text WANTED.

proof.text: For $g:S'\to S$, compare $D_S(\mathcal M)\times_SS'$ and $D_{S'}(g^{-1}\mathcal M)$ on the pullback of a lattice-trivializing cover. By constant pullback and Step 1 both are the same split torus, with the same inverse-dual transition matrix. The identity maps on the split models therefore glue uniquely to an isomorphism. Similarly there is a natural comparison $g^{-1}X^*(P)\to X^*(P_{S'})$, induced by pulling back characters. After pulling back a splitting cover of $P$, constant pullback and the split matrix lemma identify this comparison with the identity of $\underline{\mathbf Z^r}$, so it is an isomorphism. On each such chart the two evaluation maps are $m\mapsto(h\mapsto h(m))$ and $p\mapsto(\chi\mapsto\chi(p))$ before and after base change. The formulas are unchanged on pulled-back tuples; hence the comparisons preserve both evaluation maps. Uniqueness of gluing gives compatibility with successive base changes. This argument uses no assertion that arbitrary inverse image carries the entire units sheaf to the units sheaf.

source.place: Agent relative descent argument, using Lemma 12.4 and Theorem 12.9(a), pp.232–234; Lan §3.1.1 local text WANTED.

proof.text: On an affine splitting chart the split model has algebra $A[x_1,y_1,\ldots,x_r,y_r]/(x_iy_i-1)_i$, a finite presentation. It is formally smooth: a tuple of units modulo a square-zero ideal lifts to a tuple of units, since a lifted product equal to $1+e$ has inverse corrected by $1-e$; assign each $y_i$ the inverse of the lifted $x_i$. Thus it is smooth by the definition, and flat and locally of finite presentation by smooth-flat. The tuple $(1,\ldots,1)$ gives a section, so the model is surjective. Over each affine open of $S$, the same finite affine refinement as Step 3 is a single flat quasi-compact surjection. Smooth fpqc base descent applies to $D$ there. Smoothness is Zariski local by its affine-local definition, so $D\to S$ is smooth globally, hence flat and locally of finite presentation. Affineness descends on these covers and is local on the target. An affine map is quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated; together with local finite presentation this is finite presentation. The identity section gives global surjectivity, hence faithful flatness. Over an algebraically closed geometric point choose a field-valued point on the pulled-back etale cover; the etale-lift factorization lemma over the separably closed geometric field gives a section of that cover. The fibre is therefore the split torus of the stalk rank. For rank zero every local model and every transition is the identity of its base; the construction gives $S$ with the trivial group. The empty base is covered by the empty family and yields the empty scheme, consistently with all assertions.
